symptom: A Mendix 10 project with a consumed REST client that has any POST/PUT/PATCH operation cannot be loaded: `mx convert` aborts with `TypeCacheUnknownTypeException: The type cache does not contain a type with qualified name Rest$JsonBody` (Studio Pro cannot open it either), while `mxcli check`, `exec` and `mx check` all pass
cause: `restBodyToGen` wrote Rest$JsonBody for every JSON body — and POST/PUT/PATCH default to a JSON body — but the type only exists from Mendix 11.0.0 (measured: 10.24.24 refuses it, 11.0.0 loads it). The doctype gate never noticed because 06-rest-client-examples.mdl is version-gated to 11.0+ as a whole (for query parameters), so no REST client was ever written to a 10.x project in CI
file: `mdl/backend/modelsdk/consumed_rest_write.go` (`restBodyForms`, `restBodyToGen`: Rest$StringBody on <11.0, its ValueTemplate on ≥10.11 and Value before); tests `mdl/backend/modelsdk/rest_body_version_test.go`; ungated doctype script `mdl-examples/doctype-tests/06c-rest-client-mendix10-examples.mdl`
insight: **`mx check` does not prove a project loads**: mxbuild tolerated a type its version does not have, while `mx convert` — Mendix's own loader — refused the project outright, so convert is the cheaper oracle for 'can Studio Pro open this'. **A whole-file version gate hides every version bug in the file**: one 11.0-only feature (query parameters) gated the whole REST showcase, so the most common construct (a POST) was never written to Mendix 10 in CI; keep an ungated script of the constructs every supported version has. Bisect a type's first version with `mxcli setup mxbuild --version X` + `mx convert` on one tiny script — 11.0.0 was one download away. Found by running the doctype corpus WITHOUT honouring `@version` directives, which is what a user on 10.24 does
